newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan CPC Taoyuan refinery restarts topping units.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan CPC Taoyuan refinery restarts topping units.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum said on Friday it had restarted the topping unit at its Taoyuan refinery that was idled by a crude port shutdown and had boosted production to 72 percent of capacity.
"The Taoyuan refinery is now running at 72 percent of full capacity, after new crude supplies flowed in on Thursday," Chinese Petroleum official Liao Pai-fong told Reuters by telephone.
The refinery's crude port was shut down on September 15 over unspecified problems, forcing the plant to reduce production to 34 percent of capacity by halting one of the two topping units.
The facility's main product is jet oil for Taiwan's main international airport, which is nearby.
The refinery has two 100,000-barrels-per-day topping or distillation units, which Liao said now were producing at rates of 75,000 and 69,000 barrels per day, Liao said.
Chinese Petroleum reopened its Taoyuan crude port late on Thursday and started pumping crude from the 300,000-tonne tanker Vanadis, aiming to complete the offloading by Sunday.
The 250,000-tonne crude tanker Felipe Camarao would begin offloading its cargo once the Vanadis is finished, a Chinese Petroleum headquarters official said.
Only one of the offshore crude port's pumping units has been repaired and reopened, but is only able to operate at half of its capacity because only one of two pipelines is open.
Officials have said it was impossible to predict when the operating unit's second pipeline could be opened or when the second unit, which also has two pipelines, would be able to operate.

Chinese Petroleum also has declined to comment on the cost of the problems or to confirm reports by industry sources that it had been compensating the tanker Vanadis at US$30,000 a day during the 16 days it waited to unload its cargo.
